note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Conflicting-objective alignment -> MGDA limits -> GAPO / P-GAPO -> theory and experiments

nodes.name: Single reward misses diverse preferences
nodes.description: Standard RLHF uses a single reward model representing average human preference, but human opinions are diverse and cannot be encapsulated in one reward.

nodes.name: Objectives conflict
nodes.description: Optimizing multiple alignment objectives such as helpfulness and harmlessness is hard because the objectives conflict; e.g. Safe RLHF often yields exaggerated safety behavior, harmless but unhelpful responses.

nodes.name: Linear scalarization is limited
nodes.description: Linear scalarization of multiple rewards is inherently limited in exploring Pareto-optimal solutions that balance trade-offs, and preference-weighted rewards exacerbate RLHF training instability.

nodes.name: MGDA finds Pareto-stationary points
nodes.description: MGDA solves min ||sum alpha_i grad J_i||^2 over the simplex; either the solution is 0 (Pareto stationary) or it gives a descent direction improving all objectives.

nodes.name: MGDA optimizes objectives at consistent rates
nodes.description: Theorem 3.1 shows MGDA's update makes all objectives improve at consistent rates, which restricts the underdeveloped objectives when one is near-optimal.

nodes.name: MGDA is dominated by small gradients
nodes.description: When gradient magnitudes differ greatly, MGDA's update direction is dominated by the objective with the smallest gradient, neglecting objectives that still need optimization; it also ignores user preferences by finding one Pareto solution.

nodes.name: GAPO gradient rescaling
nodes.description: GAPO normalizes each objective's gradient by the p-th power of its L2 norm (p=1 standard normalization, p=2 reciprocal-length rescaling) before solving the MGDA problem, to mitigate gradient scale disparities.

nodes.name: GAPO descent and proportional rates
nodes.description: Theorem 3.2 shows GAPO's direction is a common descent direction for all objectives unless Pareto stationary, and Theorem 3.3 shows objective improvement is proportional to the p-th power of gradient L2 norm, focusing on underdeveloped objectives with larger gradients.

nodes.name: P-GAPO user preferences
nodes.description: P-GAPO normalizes gradients with p=1 and takes a preference-weighted sum with user preference vector lambda, so the update prioritizes preferred objectives and yields Pareto solutions matching user needs.

nodes.name: Practical implementation
nodes.description: GAPO is implemented over PPO using only the last-layer policy gradients to avoid the m*n space cost of full gradients.

nodes.name: Single-objective PPO fails the other objective
nodes.description: PPO-H and PPO-S reach the best score on one dimension but perform poorly on the other (PPO-S refuses most prompts), motivating multi-objective alignment.

nodes.name: Safe RLHF under-optimizes harmlessness
nodes.description: Safe RLHF gives only small harmlessness improvement because the SFT model is already near its safety constraint, so PPO-Lagrangian rapidly shrinks the harmlessness weight.

nodes.name: GAPO best balance
nodes.description: On Mistral-7B with PKU-SafeRLHF and HH-RLHF, GAPO (p=1 and p=2) achieve the best and second-best average of helpfulness and harmlessness, keeping PPO-H-level helpfulness with high harmlessness.

nodes.name: GAPO p=1 wins GPT-4o evaluation
nodes.description: In GPT-4o pairwise evaluation against the SFT model, GAPO p=1 outperforms Safe RLHF, is competitive with PPO-H and PPO-S, and significantly surpasses p=2.

nodes.name: P-GAPO front beats RS and MORLHF
nodes.description: P-GAPO outperforms MORLHF when preferences are balanced (lambda 0.4-0.6), MORLHF is slightly better at extreme preferences, and the P-GAPO and MORLHF fronts completely dominate Rewarded Soups.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from conflicting-objective alignment limits of single reward, linear scalarization and MGDA, through the GAPO/P-GAPO method and theorems, to experimental validation.
